answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with collateral-backed spot-audit escrow. Each identity locks a refundable deposit, recorded on a public ledge, before claiming work. Auditors wander through recent jobs to verify the work was done. A fake identity earns nothing until it passes, so an attacker must fund every copy separately, while honest agents recover their deposit over time. Cheating forfeits the deposit and leaves an umber mark that makes future work harder to win. Since cost scales per copy and audits are unpredictable, mass fake identities become expensive and pointless.
